title: How do you clear the decimal in the divisor?
text: $$0.3$$ has one decimal place. Multiply the divisor and the dividend by 10, which moves both decimal points one place to the right. A common mistake is to move the point in only one of the numbers. $$0.3 \times 10 = 3$$. What is $$3.6 \times 10$$?

title: Divide the whole numbers
text: The problem is now $$36 \div 3$$. What is that quotient?

title: Worked solution
text: $$3.6 \div 0.3 = 36 \div 3 = 12$$. Check: $$0.3 \times 12 = 3.6$$. Common mistake: answering $$1.2$$ by dividing 3.6 by 3 without moving the dividend's decimal point. General rule: multiply the divisor and the dividend by the same power of 10 so the divisor is a whole number, then divide.
